# Duewise review for a reusable MAUI starter kit

Reviewed **2026-10-21** by source/document inspection. Baseline: `de41ba0e4749609f2bd78b01021089673186bdfc`; the working tree was clean before this documentation task. No application code, dependencies, build settings, workflow, or signing files are changed by the kit.

Scope: architecture and development/documentation patterns suitable for reuse. This is a targeted review, not an exhaustive defect, performance, or security audit. Governing behavior remains [PRD R01-R08 and authorized extensions](../../PRD.md), with technical contracts in [SDD](../../SDD.md). The kit is future-project material and does not authorize Duewise platform expansion or close its release gates.

## Key findings and priority

Priorities below apply when starting the next project. They are recommendations, not newly approved Duewise backlog items.

| Priority | Finding and evidence | Improvement / consequence |
|---|---|---|
| 1: before scaffolding | The [App project](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/DueDateChecker.App.csproj) targets only `net10.0-android`, minimum OS 26. [MauiProgram](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/MauiProgram.cs) registers the Android reminder implementation directly. [PRD](../../PRD.md) specifies Android delivery. | Declare target platforms/capabilities first; adding TFMs alone is insufficient. Isolate native registrations and design each required adapter before claiming multi-platform support. |
| 1: before shared builds | No repository `global.json`, `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Packages.props`, `.editorconfig`, or NuGet package lock file was found. MAUI Controls uses workload-supplied `$(MauiVersion)`; [CI](../../../.github/workflows/ci.yml) selects SDK `10.0.x`. | Pin and record compatible SDK/workload/native tools; add consistent formatting/analyzer settings and a deliberate restore policy. Central package management is optional, not a prerequisite. |
| 1: before relying on CI | [CI](../../../.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs Core and source-linked App tests on Linux on push, with no PR trigger or MAUI App build. [STATUS](../../delivery/STATUS.md) says CI activation is held and has no observed GitHub run. | For a new shipping project, add merge validation and host-appropriate App target builds. Establish an actual remote passing run. Do not infer GitHub state from a checked-in workflow. |
| 1: before release | [STATUS](../../delivery/STATUS.md#remaining-release-work) leaves intended-key/native acceptance open. [Signing example](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/local.signing.props.example) uses a developer-specific path. | Use placeholders/secure injected signing configuration and verify the artifact's signing identity. Build success or a `Signed.apk` filename cannot close R01. Actual local signing secrets were not inspected. |
| 2: during first slices | [App.Tests](../../../tests/DueDateChecker.App.Tests/DueDateChecker.App.Tests.csproj) links ViewModels and selected Services into a plain .NET test assembly. It does not reference/build the MAUI App assembly. | Retain this practical small-app approach with an explicit source list and compiler/package parity. Extract a Presentation project when source-link maintenance becomes significant. Neither arrangement replaces native testing. |
| 2: before localization | [CalendarViewModel](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/ViewModels/CalendarViewModel.cs) and [DueListItem](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/ViewModels/DueListItem.cs) use English/invariant presentation and Manila policy. [DashboardViewModel](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/ViewModels/DashboardViewModel.cs) compares filter strings with display status/category labels. | These fit the current product. For another locale, separate typed keys from resource strings, define plurals/display culture, and centralize a date policy if multiple consumers need it. Translating a label must not alter filtering. |
| 2: while adding services | Dashboard/Calendar catch errors and retain stale data, but discard exception details; [MauiProgram](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/MauiProgram.cs) only adds a debug logging provider. Inspected source contains no `ILogger`/LogError-style usage. | Define safe diagnostic categories/event IDs and sink/retention policy. Preserve friendly UI errors while enabling diagnosis; omit user financial content and secrets. |
| 2: while adding lifecycle work | [DatabaseDispatcher](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/Services/DatabaseDispatcher.cs) serializes background work but accepts no cancellation token. [CalendarPage](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/Pages/CalendarPage.xaml.cs) coalesces loads and starts/stops its date timer on appearance/disappearance. [App](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/App.xaml.cs) owns resume handlers. | Document operation/timer/subscription ownership, stopping/resume behavior, cancellation or stale-response suppression, and multi-window scope for a new app. These observations identify design work, not a demonstrated race or leak. |
| 2: before schema changes | [DatabaseInitializer](../../../src/DueDateChecker.Core/Data/DatabaseInitializer.cs) transacts each migration with its version update and rejects newer schemas. [STATUS](../../delivery/STATUS.md#remaining-release-work) still calls out mid-script rollback and explicit repository equal-date ordering coverage. | Preserve data-safety patterns and add tests for meaningful gaps. Test released-schema upgrades, partial failure, repeat initialization, query ties, and downgrade limits. |
| 2: during documentation setup | The [root README](../../../README.md) still describes reminders as excluded and an old display title; [PRD F05](../../PRD.md#f05-reminder-rules) and [App project](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/DueDateChecker.App.csproj) show authorized reminders and `Duewise`. DESIGN retains broad concepts behind an explicit scope notice. | Keep the new root README focused on links and a short current overview. Separate future design concepts from adopted rules. Record this existing discrepancy here; no product behavior is silently re-scoped. |
| 3: when scale justifies it | Core contains Domain and SQLite Data in one assembly; [SDD](../../SDD.md#4-architecture) explicitly calls this a convention. Dashboard/Calendar load snapshots and filter/count in memory. | Keep the simple split for modest data. Add enforceable Infrastructure/Presentation boundaries, paging or caching only for concrete maintenance/scale needs; no performance failure was measured. |

## Patterns worth reusing

| Pattern | Inspected implementation and tests | Reuse boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Small solution with testable rules | [Solution](../../../DueDateChecker.slnx), [Core project](../../../src/DueDateChecker.Core/DueDateChecker.Core.csproj), [Core tests](../../../tests/DueDateChecker.Core.Tests/DueDateChecker.Core.Tests.csproj) | Domain stays free of MAUI; Data implements contracts. Raw SQL is a project choice, not a universal default. |
| MVVM with explicit states | [DashboardViewModel](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/ViewModels/DashboardViewModel.cs), [CalendarViewModel](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/ViewModels/CalendarViewModel.cs), [Dashboard tests](../../../tests/DueDateChecker.App.Tests/DashboardTests.cs), [Calendar tests](../../../tests/DueDateChecker.App.Tests/CalendarTests.cs) | Generated properties/commands, injected clock, read-only collections, stale data and distinct empty states are useful patterns. Test bodies were inspected; not rerun here. |
| Clear native UI boundary | [Detail page](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/Pages/DueDetailPage.xaml.cs), [Shell](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/AppShell.xaml.cs), [Calendar page](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/Pages/CalendarPage.xaml.cs) | Pages handle routes/native controls; view models handle state. ID-only queries and navigation guards avoid moving mutable records through routes. |
| DI and resource-aware startup | [MauiProgram](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/MauiProgram.cs), [App](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/App.xaml.cs), [SDD lifetimes](../../SDD.md#7-dependency-lifetimes-and-startup) | Construct resources/theme before pages; share repositories/clock and use fresh editor drafts. Shell can retain a page registered transiently. |
| Explicit SQLite execution boundary | [Dispatcher](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/Services/DatabaseDispatcher.cs), [repository](../../../src/DueDateChecker.Core/Data/SqliteDueRepository.cs) | Background serialized work addresses this provider's synchronous execution; parameterized values and active-row update guards protect mutations. Generalize to the selected provider and concurrency needs. |
| Data-preserving tests | [Repository tests](../../../tests/DueDateChecker.Core.Tests/SqliteDueRepositoryTests.cs), [category tests](../../../tests/DueDateChecker.Core.Tests/CategoryTests.cs), [create/list tests](../../../tests/DueDateChecker.App.Tests/CreateAndListTests.cs), [delete tests](../../../tests/DueDateChecker.App.Tests/DeleteDueTests.cs) | Temporary real SQLite files, reopen/retry/idempotency tests, schema preservation and controlled failures exercise behavior beyond mocks. |
| Durable state separated from OS scheduling | [Reminder ADR](../../adr/007-local-reminder-reconciliation.md), [platform contract](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/Services/IReminderPlatform.cs), [Android receiver/job](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/Platforms/Android/ReminderReceiver.cs) | Durable source-of-truth/reconciliation is reusable when needed. Android scheduling/power semantics and product reminder defaults are not portable defaults. |
| Traceable delivery documentation | [Documentation index](../../README.md), [soft-delete spec](../../../specs/v1.3-soft-delete/spec.md), [plan](../../../specs/v1.3-soft-delete/plan.md), [tasks](../../../specs/v1.3-soft-delete/tasks.md) | Stable requirements, observable scenarios, separate plans/tasks, and attributed evidence are the kit's foundation. |
| Controlled native verification | [Verification tools guide](../../../tools/verification/README.md) | Explicit devices, synthetic fixtures, sanitized output and restored settings are useful practices; app-specific fixture/serial assumptions must be replaced. |

## Documented, implemented, and verified

- **Documented intent:** R01-R08 establish local Android delivery, persistence and optional CI; later F01/F02/F03/F04/F05/F07 extend it through PRD/spec links. [DESIGN's scope notice](../../DESIGN.md#scope-and-authority) prevents its iOS/future concepts from becoming automatic requirements.
- **Implemented/source-observed here:** Android-only App plus platform-independent Core, MVVM/DI/Shell, SQLite migrations, saved-data Dashboard/Calendar, categories/preferences and Android reminder integration. Source presence establishes none of their runtime acceptance in this review.
- **Historical verification:** [STATUS](../../delivery/STATUS.md) records 61 Core + 155 App cases passed and a zero-warning/error Android Release build on 2026-10-18 for F04. Its native restoration/acceptance state and previous feature evidence remain artifact-specific. These are existing attributed records, not freshly reproduced results.
- **Fresh verification in this task:** documentation/source inspection, official-reference review, and the documentation checks recorded below. No restore, build, application tests, device use, GitHub run inspection, package vulnerability scan, or signing verification was performed.

## Product-specific choices to replace

Do not carry over PHP/centavo rules, Asia/Manila, the fixed category taxonomy, Paid status rules, soft deletion without restore, reminder schedules/permissions, offline-only scope, Android-only targeting, API 26, single-window assumptions, app-private unencrypted SQLite with disabled backup, package ID/signing key, branding, or historical approvals. Select them explicitly for the next product. The [manifest](../../../src/DueDateChecker.App/Platforms/Android/AndroidManifest.xml) also contains network permissions; review each required permission for the next application rather than copying the manifest wholesale.

Reusable design/engineering guidance is in [STRUCTURE](STRUCTURE.md), [DEVELOPMENT](project/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md), and the [official references](project/docs/REFERENCES.md). Source-specific toolchain values describe this repository; SETUP placeholders require a new compatibility decision.

## Documentation validation evidence

Status: **Passed, agent-observed on 2026-10-21**. Environment: Windows/PowerShell with a Python standard-library Markdown checker and Git in the repository workspace; source baseline above. Artifact: the 23 Markdown files under this kit plus the added navigation in `docs/README.md`.

| Check | Observed outcome |
|---|---|
| Local Markdown paths and heading anchors | 24 documents checked; all 242 local links resolve, including 7 heading-anchor references. Fenced examples are excluded from link parsing. |
| Portability of the copyable tree | All 87 local links originating in `project/` resolve inside that tree; no source-repository file is required after copying. |
| Required materials and template integrity | All 19 project-template files present; placeholders balanced; no prechecked tasks, reference-app identity or copied test counts in the copyable tree. |
| External technical references | 12 distinct official URLs opened/reviewed for the cited guidance; version-sensitive details are dated and adoption requires revalidation. No recursive external-site link audit was attempted. |
| Authority and traceability review | Requirement/contract ownership, feature scenarios and implementation/build/device/acceptance separation reviewed; current Duewise lessons map to kit destinations above. |
| Whitespace, conflict markers and final diff | `git diff --check` passed; new files also checked for trailing whitespace, conflict markers and final newlines. |
| Preservation and change scope | Only existing tracked file changed: `docs/README.md`, with seven added lines. All 23 new files are under the requested kit path. No staged changes or other untracked changes; application and historical files preserved. |

The initial content check prompted removal of two reference-app mentions from portable workflow/standards prose; the corrected tree passed. No application restore, tests, builds, native checks, or release acceptance were performed or inferred. The checker validates conventional inline Markdown paths/heading anchors, not visual rendering of every table/diagram.
